newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks record new gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks record new gains at close.

text.p: Argentina's bullish stock market extended gains on speculative buying Thursday, with players hunting for bargains among issues which lagged the blue-chip index in September, dealers said.

"The market just keeps pushing higher because underlying sentiment is very good and many stocks are just now waking up to that fact, led by the highly liquid telephone sector," said Humberto Lopez at Wainbuch traders.
The weighted MerVal index .MERV tacked on 0.9 percent to close at 575.38, boosting gains so far in the week to 3.5 percent after a 10 percent rise in September.
But traders predicted the market might soon retrench -- especially if employment data comes in stronger than expected Friday in the United States and rattles Wall Street.

"We may soon be a bit on the defensive because it's hard to keep up this pace of gains," said Lopez, noting volume would have to stay at new healthier levels in order to underpin the market short-term.

Floor turnover grew to 23.5 million pesos from 21.6 million Wednesday, when volume soared from a recent average tally of 13 million, while over-the-counter deals were virtually unchanged at 128.8 million pesos.

In the medium term, analysts said the outlook was firm based on steady economic recovery and Argentina's successful attempts at foreign financing, including this week's $1.0 billion global bond issue.
"The support of the IMF is also a key factor and the bolsa has drawn strength from (Economy Minister Roque) Fernandez's trip to Washington this week," said dealer Emilio Alessandro.

Fernandez said Thursday he was confident the International Monetary Fund would approve a letter of intent raising Argentina's fiscal deficit ceiling this year to $6.0 billion against an original target of $2.5 billion.
In the session the broad market rose 1.0 percent, with winners beating losers 42 to nine and 21 issues closing flat.
Among main-tier stocks, Telecom and Telefonica rose another 1.9 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively, after each surging 4.0 percent Wednesday.
Top MerVal gains were in sugar refiner Ledesma, holding company Comercial del Plata and Bansud, which jumped 3.3 percent, 2.9 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively.
Heaviest losers were steelmaker Siderca, which slipped 2.0 percent, and construction stock Polledo, off 1.9 percent.
